integrity: The proof reduces the centered Gaussian sample to an isotropic Gaussian on the residual subspace, factors it into independent chi radius and uniform direction, and observes that degree-q weighting multiplies the radial density by r^q. The resulting radial law is exactly chi with q additional degrees of freedom. The packaged checker verifies the implied moment identities across integer and noninteger degree shifts; it is supplementary to the analytic proof.
scientific_limitations: The exact chi-square dimension shift uses the normal residual radius-direction factorization and is not asserted for general elliptical or nonnormal samples.
The theorem determines the radial law under homogeneous size-biasing but not the tilted angular distribution beyond its density proportional to the statistic on the residual sphere.
For concrete statistics such as the sample range, the covariance identity can still involve a classical expectation without an elementary closed form.
title: Homogeneous Gaussian dispersion bias adds exactly its degree to residual chi-square dimension
